normalized.quote: Enron Energy Services recorded its first profitable quarter as expected at the end of 1999, and continued to grow rapidly through 2000, with increasing profits in all four quarters of 2000 and aggregate recurring income before interest and taxes (IBIT) of $103 million for the year.
normalized.why: This can be verified by checking the $103 million income figure for 2000.

normalized.quote: The value of our contracts in 2000 totaled more than $16 billion, increasing Enron Energy Services’ cumulative contract value to more than $30 billion since late 1997.
normalized.why: The $16 billion and $30 billion contract values can be checked against financial records.

normalized.quote: Additionally, 2000 was marked by increased activity in Europe – an untapped market for energy outsourcing.
normalized.why: The claim of increased activity in Europe during the year 2000 is verifiable.

normalized.quote: Retail energy earnings will be fueled by the rapid growth of our U.S. and European businesses and the strong execution and extension of existing contracts.
normalized.why: This can be checked by reviewing regional business growth and contract execution in 2001.

normalized.quote: Our comprehensive energy out-sourcing product has proven an exceptionally effective way for companies to reduce their costs, manage risks of energy price volatility, improve their energy infrastructure and focus resources on their core businesses.
normalized.why: It lacks specific factual anchors and relies on subjective praise of the outsourcing product.

normalized.quote: This success reflects growing acceptance of Enron’s energy outsourcing product – acceptance that has meant an increasing rate of new contracting.
normalized.why: It is a vague statement relying on unquantified success and acceptance without specific metrics.

normalized.quote: Our retail energy success in 2000 also reflects our strong emphasis on contract execution and implementation and on excellence in customer service.
normalized.why: Names a date (in 2000) that a reader can check against a public source.
